paper.title: Exponential Regret Bounds for Gaussian Process Bandits with Deterministic Observations

settings.name_in_paper: Gaussian process bandits with deterministic observations
unmapped: Objective f is a sample from a zero-mean GP prior with known kernel hyperparameters; kernel four times differentiable along the diagonal (applies to SE and Matern nu>=2); not stated via information gain
Learner samples only from a fixed finite lattice L in D
settings.definition_quote: Let f : D → R be a function on a compact subset D ⊆ R^d ... our assumption is that once the function has been probed at point x ∈ D, then the value f(x) can be observed with very high precision. ... the objective function is distributed according to a Gaussian process prior: f(x) ∼ GP(m(·), κ(·, ·)).

algorithms.name: Branch and Bound (GP-UCB/LCB with search-space shrinking)

symbols.A: positive constant depending on the instance
symbols.tau: positive decay rate depending on behaviour of f near its maximum
symbols.T_0: integer threshold (paper's T) after which bound holds

conditions: kernel four times differentiable along the diagonal

f continuous sample with unique global maximum x_M satisfying either (†) interior quadratic behaviour c2||x-xM||^2 <= f(xM)-f(x) < c1||x-xM||^2 on B(xM,rho0), or (‡) xM on boundary, f and ∂D smooth at xM with nonzero gradient
lattice L satisfies 2L ∩ conv(L) ⊆ L and is fine enough (condition (5))
tuning: beta_T = 2 ln(|L| T^2 / alpha), alpha in (0,1)

source.quote: Then, there exist positive numbers A and τ and an integer T such that the points specified by the Branch and Bound algorithm, {x_t}, will satisfy the following asymptotic bound: For all t > T, with probability 1 − α we have r(x_t) < A e^{-τt/(ln t)^{d/4}}.

results.notes: Bound is on the instantaneous regret r(x_t)=f(x_M)-f(x_t), not cumulative; quantity 'other'. Holds with probability 1-alpha (alpha is the algorithm's confidence parameter). Constants A, tau, T depend on instance and lattice.

conditions: same conditions as Theorem 2 on kernel, f and lattice L
tuning: beta_T = 2 ln(|L| T^2 / alpha), alpha in (0,1)

source.quote: Given κ, f ∼ GP(0, κ) and L ⊆ D as in Theorem 2, the cumulative regret is bounded from above.

results.notes: Qualitative statement: cumulative regret bounded (constant in T). Probability type not explicitly stated; inherited from Theorem 2 (probability 1-alpha).
